adaptations.reason: Distinguish structural closure, committed data boundaries, local query ownership and interaction readiness in an evaluation-scoped snapshot without mutating shared native values
adaptations.observable: Existing syntax marks remain private; per-property/index boundaries and query dependencies live outside protocol values and serialized ASTs. Parser/native baselines are separate from evaluation snapshots; old native projections remain immutable while SameValue and reverse encoding retain JS identity. Each descendant constraints travel with that output occurrence through core prop-array copies; native projection memoizes by value identity and scope, so unrelated occurrences of a shared native graph remain independent without cloning Lang values. Dependency-free open/closed presentation descriptions are frozen shared metadata, recognized directly by the Swift bridge; query, occurrence, placeholder and structural metadata remain distinct. Completed parser ASTs with closed, reference-free syntax retain only their context-independent closure/depth fact in a weak map; no Lang value, diagnostic, default or function result is cached and alias depth remains checked. Recursive query discovery reuses the same reference-free closure fact after following a symbol reference; materialized values retain fresh identity
adaptations.verification: Strict intermediate snapshots, independent document and synchronous nested-evaluation scopes, same-evaluation shared-graph sibling/Each/query isolation, immutable native projections with preserved JS identity and opaque action captures, bounded scope memoization and preserved output-budget rejection, native alias readiness regressions, source-tail boundary tests, staged chart/table and complete-control/incomplete-action UI tests, frozen presentation defaults and exact stable-sibling description counts, zero settled-literal descendant enumeration during changing-tail query discovery with fresh element/container identities
adaptations.removal: Upstream exposes equivalent source/dependency provenance; injection is explicitly retained until then

adaptations.observable: Private failure metadata reaches Swift before any rejected diagnostic/state/default/root graph is projected. adaptations.verification: Alias-depth, repeated-subtree, single and cumulative expression-default regressions; no null-default tool dispatch; an 8192-unknown-call error graph is rejected before native enumeration while ordinary diagnostics remain intact; separate from strict equivalence cases

adaptations.reason: Bound dynamic Each, recursive evaluation, builtin work, implicit primitive conversions, string growth, and expanded native/render output before large allocations or tool dispatch
adaptations.observable: 100000 work units and expanded value nodes, 256 levels, 4096 element occurrences and 1048576 UTF16 output units; repeated aliases add cached subtree cost rather than bypassing the budget. Private bridge evaluation/query entries report work and accept a smaller remaining native action allowance; nested calls share the existing scope. Recoverable reports and root diagnostics share a cumulative bounded output channel and consume work, including each native error envelope's fields and nodes. Terminal exception text is checked before its error envelope is built. MCP extraction checks the expanded result after the official helper parses text as JSON and explicitly rejects excess before Swift projection. Public core API values, parameters and callback ordering stay unchanged. Evaluation exhaustion preserves the previous bounded presentation and retires execution; standalone MCP extraction reports MCPToolError
adaptations.verification: Normal and excessive nested Each, DAG occurrence counting, implicit comparison/index/action coercion and cumulative builtin conversion work, string growth, automatic Query reevaluation, individually allowed defaults that exceed one batch, borrowed remaining work and nested non-resetting scopes, synchronous invalidation notification work, three individually allowed 500000-unit reports and short diagnostic envelopes, cumulative root diagnostics and oversized exception text, native action side-effect regressions, and MCP text/structured-output depth/node limits with independent recovery

adaptations.reason: An exception escaping a native runtime entry or automatic query reader must not cross JavaScriptCore as an undefined success value
adaptations.observable: Private bounded entries return an explicit runtime diagnostic distinct from a budget outcome. Owners retain one first failure, retire execution and preserve the last presentation; nested scopes cannot hide an inner failure. Automatic readers report and dispose before dependent dispatch. Official recoverable prop/function diagnostics keep their existing behavior. Malformed MCP envelopes use the existing MCPToolError channel. Public signatures and nativeLimitExceeded budget-only meaning remain
adaptations.verification: Initial and asynchronous query coercion, direct and nested expression failure, no later provider/action work, recovery after source replacement, unaffected recoverable root props, and malformed MCP extraction followed by a valid result
adaptations.removal: Equivalent explicit shared-core/native execution failure transport

adaptations.reason: Check provider results and failure payloads, MCP JSON envelopes, explicit query/mutation inputs, evaluation-context values, public Evaluator ASTs and high-level State writes/restoration before their JavaScriptCore allocation; this is a native transport boundary separate from the JS execution/output guard
adaptations.observable: Plain-data limits match expanded JS output cost: 100000 nodes, 256 container levels, 4096 element occurrences and 1048576 UTF16 key/value units. Immutable DAG costs are memoized but charged at every occurrence. MCP JSONValue input uses the same aggregate native cost before encoding; provider failure messages, available-tool lists and native custom-function error descriptions are checked before JS allocation. Store aggregate accounting follows actual snapshot changes, preserving the old cost after an upstream shallow no-op without overwriting accepted reentrant writes or pristine. Native readiness, action/transport ASTs and captures are conservatively charged even when hidden or simplified by encoding; this narrows the accepted native transport domain without changing normal Lang results. Callback failure retires the evaluator and poisons the active JS budget with its private token, preventing later native callbacks; positive input caches are weak, context-local and bounded
adaptations.verification: Native wide/deep/shared-graph, UTF16, action/binding/readiness, direct/nested opaque captures, aggregate extra-scope/persisted-state, MCP JSON input, aggregate provider-failure payload and weak-cache tests; JS callback/prop/query failure-token regressions assert no later dispatch and independent-scope recovery

adaptations.reason: Native timers, controlled tools and disposal; raw query statements and live evaluation context delegate dependency scheduling to the official QueryManager
adaptations.observable: Callbacks, in-flight replacement and cancellation; retiring a mutation cancels and rejects only that incarnation's pending requests, even if its provider ignores cancellation. A private query validity predicate captures the existing cache entry and checks that a current query still consumes its key, so native preflight and completion share the same validity check. After a complete query update, native pending requests that are no longer valid are cancelled and rejected; shared requests with current consumers remain active
adaptations.verification: Controlled official manager traces, native bridge tests, never-settling provider retirement, replacement mutation, queued-query key/entry replacement and unchanged-key preservation, same-patch cross-id handoff, separate delete/recreate, shared-request consumer retirement, and unrelated-query lifecycle regressions
adaptations.removal: Equivalent Apple async execution integration

adaptations.reason: A retired query's completion must not change a replacement with the same statement id and key; shared requests must continue when another query still consumes their cache entry
adaptations.observable: Success, errors, finalization and native validity use the existing cache entry identity and current consumers. Shared consumers agree on loading/result/error state, clear obsolete previous-key references together, and request at most one pending refresh for the shared key. Fetch success and successful cache adoption share error/previous-key cleanup. During a query patch, removed or overwritten cache references are collected in a function-local set and cleaned only after every node is updated, preserving current/shared/previous consumers while releasing orphaned results. Disposal builds its own retained terminal snapshot without depending on late request completion. No public API or separate request registry is introduced
adaptations.verification: Shipped-core controlled promises cover stale success/failure/finally, remove-all/recreate, key changes, cross-id request sharing, initiator retirement, shared retry, overwritten previous-cache retention, same-patch pending/completed cache handoff, shared/fallback preservation, successful cache adoption, invalidation and disposal snapshot consistency
adaptations.removal: Pinned upstream QueryManager passes the same lifecycle regressions
